gps.title: GPS Navigator

steps: Press "POWER". Wait for the start screen (ROM OK, RAM OK) to clear.
Press "DISPLAY SEL" until the SATELLITE page shows. Wait for FIX: 3D, at least 4 SATS used and a low HDOP.
On the SATELLITE page, filled circles are satellites in use. Hollow circles are tracked but not used. SBAS ON PRN129 means differential corrections are in use.
Check the header line: date, time, fix mode (3D, 2D, DR or --) and HDOP. A 'W' under the fix mode means SBAS is in use.
Optional: "MENU ESC" ▸ SELF TEST. Check that GPS RECEIVER and ANTENNA CURRENT read OK, then press "CLEAR" to go back.
Press "MENU ESC" ▸ GPS SETUP. Use ▲▼ to select a line and ◀▶ to change its value.
Set DATUM to WGS84 to match the charts and ECDIS. The unit starts on LUZON 1911, which puts the position hundreds of metres off.
Check FIX MODE 2D/3D, SBAS (WAAS/MSAS) ON, SMOOTHING POSITION and SPEED, and ELEVATION MASK about 5°. Press "NU/CU ENT" or "MENU ESC" to exit.
"MENU ESC" ▸ SYSTEM SETUP: set TIME DISPLAY to LOCAL and TIME OFFSET to +8.0 h for the Philippines, or keep UTC.
In SYSTEM SETUP, check UNITS (NM) and BEARING TRUE. If you choose MAG, set MAG VARIATION (− = West).
Read the position on the NAV DATA page and type it into the POSITION REPORT card (format 14 23.456 N / 120 43.210 E).
Press "WPT RTE" ▸ WAYPOINTS, then select "+ NEW WAYPOINT (own ship)" and press "NU/CU ENT".
The NEW WAYPOINT page opens with own ship's position already filled in. Overwrite it with the passage-plan position.
NAME (6 characters): ▲▼ change the letter, ◀▶ move the cursor.
LATITUDE and LONGITUDE: type digits with the numbered keys (1–9, 0). The cursor moves on by itself. On the N/S or E/W cell, ▲▼ toggles the hemisphere.
"CLEAR" blanks the digit under the cursor. Check the FROM OWN SHIP bearing and distance to make sure the position makes sense.
Press "NU/CU ENT" to save (the screen shows SAVED). "INVALID POSITION" means minutes are 60 or more. "MENU ESC" cancels.
To change a waypoint, select it in the list and press ENT, then choose EDIT, GOTO or DELETE. You cannot delete a waypoint that a route uses.
Press "WPT RTE" ▸ ROUTES. Use ▲▼ to choose an empty route (R01–R10), then press "NU/CU ENT" to edit it.
In ROUTE EDIT, ▲▼ selects a line (01–12) and ◀▶ steps through the stored waypoints to fill it.
Fill the lines in order, for example WP01 to WP04. Check the course and distance shown for each leg and the TOTAL in the title bar.
"CLEAR" deletes the waypoint on the selected line. Press "NU/CU ENT" to save (ROUTE R01 SAVED). "MENU ESC" cancels.
Press "GOTO". The menu offers CURSOR POSITION, WAYPOINT, ROUTE, MOB POSITION (after an MOB) and CANCEL GOTO.
ROUTE: select the route and press ENT. In the ROUTE LIST you can also press "GOTO" on the highlighted route.
Navigation starts from the present position to the first waypoint. It moves to the next waypoint automatically inside the arrival radius (0.10 NM if the arrival alarm is OFF).
Watch the NAV DATA page: TO and NEXT, BRG, RNG, XTE (R/L), ROUTE DIST and ROUTE ETA. HIGHWAY and STEERING show steering pictures; STEERING also shows TTG.
GOTO CURSOR: press "CURSOR ON/OFF" (switches to PLOTTER), move the cursor with the arrow pad, then press "GOTO" ▸ CURSOR POSITION.
To stop navigating, press "GOTO" ▸ CANCEL GOTO. The instructor 'Autopilot steers to GPS waypoint' box lets the ship follow the track.
"MENU ESC" ▸ ALARMS: set ARRIVAL ALARM ON with ARRIVAL RADIUS 0.30 NM, and XTE ALARM ON with XTE LIMIT 0.20 NM.
SPEED ALARM with OVER SPEED limit, and BUZZER / KEY BEEP, are on the same page.
Anchor watch (Scenario 2): set ANCHOR RADIUS (e.g. 0.10 NM), then switch ANCHOR WATCH ON. The present position becomes the anchor position. The plotter shows a dashed circle with ⚓.
When an alarm box appears ('⚠ … Press CLEAR to silence'), press "CLEAR". The XTE, anchor, NO FIX and HDOP alarms stay as CAUTION until the cause clears.
Review alarm history in "MENU ESC" ▸ MESSAGES (ALARM LOG). Scroll with ▲▼; "CLEAR" goes back.
PLOTTER page: "ZOOM IN" and "ZOOM OUT" change the scale (0.125–32 NM). "CENTER" re-centres on own ship. The arrow pad scrolls the chart.
"NU/CU ENT" toggles NORTH UP and COURSE UP. "PLOT ON/OFF" starts or stops the track. "MARK" drops a × at own ship, or at the cursor if it is on.
Clear the track or marks in "MENU ESC" ▸ PLOTTER / TRACK: select the line and press ▶.
EVENT: a short press of "EVENT MOB" saves the present position as waypoint EVT001, EVT002 and so on.
MAN OVERBOARD: press and hold "EVENT MOB" for at least 1.5 s (or hold M). The MOB position is saved, GOTO MOB starts and the STEERING page shows ★ MAN OVERBOARD ★.
Steer to the MOB using the STEERING page's BRG and RNG. To navigate to it again later, use "GOTO" ▸ MOB POSITION.
Antenna fail or Jamming: satellites are lost and 'NO POSITION FIX — DR' sounds. Press "CLEAR". The position shown is now dead reckoning (DR).
After a no-fix alarm, tell the Master and fix by radar or visual bearings. For an antenna fail, SELF TEST shows ANTENNA NG and 0 mA.
Poor geometry: HDOP rises above 4 ('HDOP … POSITION CAUTION') and the fix may drop to 2D. Press "CLEAR" and cross-check the position with radar and visual fixes.
Spoofing: no alarm sounds. The fix stays 3D with a good HDOP but drifts slowly off position. Detect it with radar ranges or visual fixes, then report it.
Press the fault button again to remove the fault. The fix returns and the NO FIX alarm clears automatically.
Cancel any active navigation with "GOTO" ▸ CANCEL GOTO if it is no longer needed.
Note the final position and time in the log book (on board).
Press "POWER". The screen blanks; waypoints, routes and settings are kept. ↺ RESTART resets the whole simulator.

tips: Keyboard shortcuts: arrow keys, Enter = ENT, Esc = MENU, Backspace = CLEAR, 0–9 = numbered keys, hold M = MOB.
In any menu, a numbered key jumps straight to that item.
COG is meaningless at or near zero speed, for example at anchor.
A 2D fix or HDOP above 4 means the position must be cross-checked.
Use ❚❚, ×1, ×5 and ×20 in the header to pause or speed up time.

ais.title: AIS Transponder

steps: Press "⏻". Wait for SELF TEST, then ROM OK RAM OK TX OK, then SYNC UTC / START TDMA.
Check the status bar: CLS A, a green TRX icon (transmitting), HIGH power, signal bars, and own MMSI 548123456.
Press "DISP" until the OWN SHIP page shows. Check POSITION, POS SOURCE EXTERNAL GNSS (DGNSS), accuracy HIGH, COG/SOG, HDG and UTC.
"MENU ESC" ▸ DIAGNOSTICS: check TX POWER 12.5 W, ANTENNA VSWR about 1.3:1 OK, and RX CH A, RX CH B and DSC OK.
"BRILL": ◀▶ adjusts brightness, "ENT ACK" toggles DAY/NIGHT, and "BRILL" again closes the window.
Press "NAV STATUS". On the VOYAGE tab, use ▲▼ to select a field and "ENT ACK" to edit it.
NAV STATUS: pick from the list (e.g. 00 UNDER WAY USING ENGINE) and press "ENT ACK".
DESTINATION: choose ENTER TEXT and use the on-screen keyboard, ending with END (SAVE). Or choose DESTINATION LIST and pick it, e.g. PH BTG.
ETA[LT]: ◀▶ moves between digits and ▲▼ changes them (DD/MM HH:MM, e.g. 01/10 22:00). "ENT ACK" saves.
TYPE OF SHIP (e.g. 70 CARGO), DRAUGHT (e.g. 08.6 m) and NO. OF PERSONS (e.g. 0022) are edited the same way.
◀▶ switches to the STATIC tab to check name, call sign, IMO, MMSI and antenna position. Static data is password-protected; report any error.
Press "MENU ESC" to leave. Update voyage data at every departure and whenever the status changes.
"MENU ESC" ▸ CPA/TCPA SETTING: ▲▼ selects a line, ◀▶ changes it.
Set CPA/TCPA ALARM ON, CPA 1.0 NM and TCPA 12 min. Keep LOST TARGET ALARM ON, and choose LIST SORT by RANGE or CPA.
"MENU ESC" ▸ DISPLAY SETTING: choose PLOTTER ORIENT. (HDG UP or NORTH UP), PLOTTER RANGE and DAY / NIGHT. "ENT ACK" or "MENU ESC" goes back.
"DISP" cycles through PLOTTER, TARGET LIST, DANGEROUS TARGETS and OWN SHIP.
PLOTTER: ▲▼ changes range (0.75–24 NM), ◀▶ selects a target, and "ENT ACK" opens its TARGET DATA. The side box shows BRG, RNG, CPA, TCPA and STATUS.
Symbols: ▲ Class A, dashed or △ Class B, ◇ AtoN, ▣ base station, ⊗ AIS-SART. A crossed symbol is a LOST TARGET.
TARGET LIST: ▲▼ moves the cursor and "ENT ACK" opens TARGET DATA. Dangerous targets are shown in red.
In TARGET DATA, compare NAV STATUS with SOG. For example, AT ANCHOR while moving at 10 kn means the other ship's data is wrong.
Report MMSIs in the WATCH REPORT card. Always confirm AIS targets by radar and visual lookout.
When 'DANGEROUS TARGET … CPA … TCPA …' appears, press "ENT ACK" to acknowledge it.
Press "DISP" until the DANGEROUS TARGETS page shows. Select the target and press "ENT ACK" to read its full data.
Check the target on radar and by sight. Call it on VHF if needed and act per COLREG. Report the MMSI in the WATCH REPORT card.
A received message flashes the MSG icon and raises 'SAFETY MESSAGE RECEIVED'. Press "ENT ACK".
"MENU ESC" ▸ MESSAGE ▸ INBOX: ▲▼ selects (✉ marks unread) and "ENT ACK" opens the message.
To send: "MENU ESC" ▸ MESSAGE ▸ CREATE MESSAGE. ▲▼ selects a line and ◀▶ changes TYPE (BROADCAST/ADDRESSED), CATEGORY (SAFETY/ROUTINE) and CHANNEL.
For ADDRESSED, select DEST MMSI and press "ENT ACK" to enter 9 digits. Select TEXT and press "ENT ACK" to type up to 156 characters.
Select [ SEND ] and press "ENT ACK". Check MESSAGE ▸ OUTBOX for SENT (MSG 14), ACK RECEIVED or NO ACK.
'AIS-SART ACTIVE MMSI 970012345' sounds the alarm (instructor: 'Trigger AIS-SART'). Press "ENT ACK".
Find the ⊗ on the PLOTTER or in the TARGET LIST. Open its data with "ENT ACK" and read MMSI, position, BRG and RNG.
Report the MMSI and bearing (within ±3°) in the WATCH REPORT card. Inform the Master, relay to MRCC or VTS, and proceed to assist (SOLAS V/33).
External GPS lost: alarm 025 EXTERNAL EPFS LOST. Press "ENT ACK", then check "MENU ESC" ▸ ALARM STATUS and SENSOR STATUS.
SENSOR STATUS should show INTERNAL GNSS IN USE, and OWN SHIP shows LOW accuracy. Report it, and expect a degraded position to be transmitted.
Gyro (HDG) lost: alarms 032 HEADING LOST / INVALID and 035 NO VALID ROT. Acknowledge them; HDG shows --- (LOST) until the gyro is restored.
Antenna VSWR: alarms 002 ANTENNA VSWR EXCEEDS LIMIT and 001 TX MALFUNCTION, and the signal bars drop. DIAGNOSTICS shows 4.2:1 NG. Other ships may not see you; inform the Master.
In ALARM STATUS, ▲▼ and "ENT ACK" acknowledge single alarms. Acknowledged alarms stay listed as ACK until the fault clears.
Silent mode, only on the Master's order: "MENU ESC" ▸ TX SETTING (SILENT MODE), ◀▶ to YES, then "ENT ACK". TRX changes to RX. Log it, and resume the same way.
(On board) AIS stays on at all times, including in port. Before berthing, set NAV STATUS to MOORED instead of switching off.
Make sure transmission is not left in silent mode.
In the simulator, press "⏻" to switch off. ↺ RESTART resets the scenario.

tips: Keyboard: arrow keys, Enter = ENT ACK, Esc = MENU, D = DISP, N = NAV STATUS, B = BRILL. Type directly on the PC keyboard when the on-screen keyboard is open.
MMSI prefixes: 548… = Philippine ship, 00548… = base station, 99548… = AtoN, 970… = AIS-SART, 111… = SAR aircraft.
AIS is an aid only; always use radar and visual lookout.
The side panel shows when the VTS message and the AIS-SART event are due.

log.title: Doppler Speed Log

steps: Press "PWR". Wait for SELF TEST..., then ROM OK RAM OK TDX OK.
"MENU" ▸ SELF TEST (ENT): check that TRANSCEIVER and TRANSDUCER read OK. Press "ENT" or "MENU" to go back.
"DIM" steps the screen brilliance (8 down to 1, then back to 8).
Press "MENU". ▲▼ selects a line, ◀▶ changes it, "ENT" confirms and "MENU" goes back.
TRACKING MODE: WATER gives STW, BOTTOM gives SOG (bottom within about 200 m), and AUTO uses bottom track when it is available.
Set SPEED AVERAGING (5/15/30/60 s), SPEED UNIT (kn, km/h, m/s) and the current CALIBRATION %.
Keep DATA OUT (VBW → RADAR/ECDIS/VDR) ON so radar, ECDIS and the VDR receive speed. KEY BEEP is optional.
"DISP" (or ◀▶ on a main page) cycles through SPEED/DISTANCE, SPEED, GRAPHIC and DATA.
The mode label shows STW (water track) or SOG (bottom track). A ▲ arrow means ahead and ▼ means astern; the SPEED page also shows AHEAD or ASTERN.
GRAPHIC shows a −5 to +20 kn bar and a 10-minute trend. DATA shows mode, signal, BT depth, trip, total, calibration and VBW output status.
Press "✱" to switch between DISTANCE (total) and TRIP.
At the start of the watch, hold "✱" for 2 s (or use MENU ▸ TRIP RESET). Select YES with ◀▶ and press "ENT".
In shallow water (38 m), set MENU ▸ TRACKING MODE to BOTTOM (or AUTO). The display then shows SOG.
Set WATER again to read STW on the same heading. Current along the heading = SOG − STW; plus is a following current.
Enter the result in the REPORTS card. Feed STW to ARPA for correct target aspect in a tideway.
Deeper than 200 m, BOTTOM gives 'BOTTOM TRACK LOST — DEPTH OUT OF RANGE'. Use WATER or AUTO there.
Going astern (engine slider below 0): read the ▼ speed on the SPEED page and report it in the REPORTS card.
"MENU" ▸ SPEED ALARM ON. Set HIGH SPEED (e.g. 10.0 kn) and, if needed, LOW SPEED (0.0 = off).
When 'HIGH SPEED ALARM > 10.0 kn' appears, press "ENT" to acknowledge it and reduce speed.
The alarm clears when speed is back inside the limits. The HI mark is shown on the GRAPHIC bar.
Press 'Measured-mile setup' (heading 090°, 12 kn, current 1.0 kn, 38 m). Use TRACKING MODE WATER and keep course and engine steady.
Press '▶ START RUN'. Run at least 1 NM by GPS, then press '■ STOP RUN'. Shorter runs are discarded.
Turn to the reciprocal course (heading 270°), steady up, then make run 2 the same way.
True STW = mean of the two GPS speeds. Correction % = (true STW ÷ mean LOG speed − 1) × 100.
Add the correction to the present value in "MENU" ▸ CALIBRATION (◀▶ in 0.1 % steps). Repeat the runs to confirm the log now agrees.
Transducer fail: 'TRANSDUCER ERROR — NO ECHO'. Speed shows --.- and SELF TEST shows TRANSDUCER NG.
Aeration / bubbles, or a rough sea: 'LOW SIGNAL (AERATION) — SPEED NOT VALID'. The speed jumps or drops out.
Press "ENT" to acknowledge. The VBW output is flagged INVALID and distance stops counting.
Tell the radar and ECDIS operators that STW is invalid. Use GPS SOG or engine RPM meanwhile, and log the fault.
Review faults in "MENU" ▸ ERROR LOG (ENT). Press the fault button again to clear the fault.
Note the TOTAL and TRIP distance in the log book if required (on board).
Press "PWR". ↺ RESTART resets the simulator.

tips: A single-axis log shows the fore-and-aft speed component only.
Keyboard: arrow keys, Enter = ENT, Esc = MENU, D = DISP, hold * = TRIP reset.
The side panel shows GPS COG/SOG as a reference.

echo.title: Echo Sounder

steps: Press "POWER". Wait for the start screen to finish (ROM OK RAM OK, TRANSDUCER FORE 50/200 kHz OK).
The unit starts in HISTORY mode on RANGE 1 (5 m) with GAIN 2, so the bottom is usually not shown yet.
Check the top bar: 'ALARM: OFF' means no shallow alarm is set yet.
Knobs: click the left or right half to turn them, or use the mouse wheel.
Turn the RANGE knob (1–8 = 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 800 m) until the bottom is inside the picture. Or press "AUTO ▼" (RANGE shows A).
Set the GAIN knob between about 2.5 and 7. Too low loses the bottom; too high gives noise and a false lock.
'NO BOTTOM LOCK' or 'BOTTOM OUT OF RANGE' means you need to change the range, gain or frequency.
"COLOR ▲" cycles BLUE, WHITE, BLACK and NIGHT. "BRILL" sets screen brilliance and "DIM" darkens the panel lamps.
"+" and "−" (outside MENU) change the picture advance speed.
Turn the MODE knob to MENU. "AUTO ▼" selects the next item, "COLOR ▲" the previous one, and "+" or "−" changes the value (hold to repeat).
Set TRANSDUCER DRAFT to the transducer depth below the waterline (8.0 m).
Set KEEL OFFSET = deepest draft − transducer depth (8.60 − 8.00 = 0.6 m).
Choose FREQUENCY: 200 kHz for shallow water and a sharp picture, 50 kHz for deep water. Also set UNITS (m/ft/fa), HISTORY SPAN and BUZZER ON.

sections.h: Set the shallow and deep alarms
steps: The alarm is referenced BELOW TRANSDUCER. Shallow depth = required UKC + (deepest draft − transducer depth).
Example: 10 % × 8.60 = 0.86 m, plus 0.60 m = 1.46 m. Set SHALLOW DEPTH to 1.5 m and SHALLOW ALARM ON.
If required, set DEEP DEPTH and DEEP ALARM ON. A red line marks each alarm depth on the echogram.
Check that the top bar shows 'ALARM: 1.5m'. Return MODE to NAV or HISTORY.
"DRAFT" cycles the reference: BELOW TRANSDUCER (DBT), BELOW SURFACE (DBS) or BELOW KEEL (DBK). The reference is shown at the bottom left.
NAV mode shows large digits, DRAFT, KEEL OFFSET and the alarm settings. DBS mode shows a full-width echogram with DEPTH BELOW SURFACE.
If DBS shows 'DRAFT 0.0 m = DBS NOT CORRECTED', enter the TRANSDUCER DRAFT.
OS DATA shows position, COG, SOG, time, DBT, DBS and DBK. HELP lists all the keys.
HISTORY mode plots the depth trend against time over the HISTORY SPAN (15/30/60 min).
LOGBOOK mode records depth, reference and position every minute. Scroll with "AUTO ▼" and "COLOR ▲".
Sounding check: expected DBS = charted depth + height of tide; expected DBT = DBS − transducer depth.
Enter both in the SOUNDING CHECK card and compare with the sounder. A large difference means checking position, chart, tide and settings.
On 'SHALLOW ALARM' (the top bar flashes red), press "MUTE ALARM". Any other key also mutes it.
Inform the Master and reduce speed to 4 kn or less with the Speed slider; less speed means less squat. Check position and chart.
The alarm clears when the depth is again greater than the set value. Muting does not change the alarm setting.
There are no fault buttons; the instructor changes conditions (sea, bottom, fish, interference) in the side panel.
Deep water (Scenario B or D): 200 kHz loses the bottom below about 150 m. Set MENU ▸ FREQUENCY to 50 kHz and use RANGE 500/800 or AUTO.
Rough sea: aeration makes the trace drop out. Reduce speed or change heading if possible, and do not trust single readings.
A weaker second trace at twice the depth is a multiple echo. Fish or interference may need a GAIN adjustment.
Record the final depth in the log book if required (on board).
Press "POWER". ↺ RESTART resets the scenario.

tips: Keyboard: ↓ = AUTO ▼, ↑ = COLOR ▲, +/− = + and −, D = DRAFT, M = MUTE ALARM, PageUp/PageDown = MODE knob.
Simulation speed starts at ×5; use ×20 or ×60 to cover the scenario faster.
A placard reminds you: the echo sounder alarm must be set at the company UKC value.

navtex.title: NAVTEX Receiver

steps: The receiver starts switched on. "⏻" toggles power; messages are received only while it is on.
Standby screen: 'NAVTEX STANDBY, Waiting for messages on 518 kHz', with the selected stations listed.
Top line: frequency, last header and ERROR RATE, then UTC and memory used (n/200).
"MENU ESC" ▸ Self Test: check that receivers, antenna and printer are OK and RESULT is NORMAL.
DIM "+" brightens and "−" dims the screen.
"MENU ESC" ▸ Frequency. ▲▼ selects and "ENT" sets 518 kHz (international, English), 490 kHz (national) or 4209.5 kHz (HF NBDP).
● marks the active frequency. Station settings are kept separately for each frequency, so set the frequency first.
"MENU ESC" ▸ Rx Setting (station / type). STATION lists the station letters for the active frequency.
Use the arrow pad to move and "ENT" to toggle [■] ON or [ ] OFF. The station name is shown at the bottom.
For a Manila → Cebu passage on 518 kHz, set M (Manila) and C (Cebu) ON and D (Davao, out of range) OFF.
Messages from stations you have not selected are not received.
On the same screen, move into MESSAGE TYPE and press "ENT" to toggle each letter.
A, B, D and L cannot be rejected; the screen shows 'cannot be rejected'.
Keep J (GNSS) ON and switch I (spare) OFF. H, C and I start OFF. Press "MENU ESC" to go back.
When 'Received new int'l msg. Display new msg ?' appears, select Yes with ◀▶ and press "ENT". "MENU ESC" cancels.
"LIST" opens the MESSAGE LIST: * = unread, ! = error. ▲▼ selects and "ENT" displays the message.
In the message, ▲▼ scrolls and "MENU ESC" goes back. Text runs from ZCZC B1B2B3B4 to NNNN.
The MESSAGE DECODER panel explains B1 station, B2 type, B3B4 serial, date-time group, error rate and the action to take.
Repeats are not stored again, except serial 00. A message with error rate above 33 % is stored as corrupt (!); wait for the repeat.
A D-type message shows 'Received SAR / DISTRESS msg!' with an audible alarm.
Press any key to silence the alarm, then select Yes and press "ENT" to read the message.
Inform the Master immediately, keep a lookout, assist if possible and report to MRCC. Record it in the GMDSS log (on board).
Keep "MENU ESC" ▸ Alarm ▸ SAR/D-type audio alarm ON ("ENT" toggles it).
"MENU ESC" ▸ Printer: "ENT" toggles Auto print ON (prints all received messages) or OFF (manual).
"PRINT" prints the message on screen. From the list it prints the highlighted message; from the main screen, the latest one.
The printout header shows frequency and error rate. '✂ TEAR OFF' clears the paper.
"MENU ESC" ▸ Send to ECDIS (MSI) lists the A, L, D and J messages.
▲▼ selects and "ENT" sends; a ✓ marks messages already sent.
In the ECDIS trainer, plot the warning with USER CH ▸ NAVTEX. Inform the OOW and the Master.
(On board) Keep NAVTEX on continuously at sea, and switch it on well before sailing so no warnings are missed.
In the simulator, press "⏻" to switch off; reception and the clock stop. ↺ RESTART clears all messages.

tips: There are no fault buttons; '⏭ NEXT MSG' jumps to the next scheduled broadcast.
Simulation time runs ×60 by default.
Keyboard: arrow keys, Enter = ENT, Esc = MENU, L = LIST, P = PRINT.
"MENU ESC" opens the MAIN MENU only from the main screen; from LIST, press it once to return to the main screen first.

pilot.title: Autopilot & Gyro Repeater

steps: Open the trainer. There is no power switch: the console is live and the clock starts at 15:00 LT.
Select simulation speed '×1' in the header. Use '❚❚' to pause and '↺ RESTART' to reset the ship to 085.1°.
Check the steering mode selector shows HAND (underlined). Ship starts on 085.1°, rudder midships, autopilot screen shows OFF.
Check the COMPASS REPEATER: outer card reads the heading at the yellow lubber line; inner fine card turns once per 10°.
Compare the repeater with the AUTO STEERING UNIT 'GYRO 1 HEADING' readout. They must agree.
Check the yellow 'GYRO ANNUAL ON' label date for service status.
Read the RUDDER ANGLE INDICATOR: dashed blue line = ORDER, yellow pointer = ACTUAL. Both should be near 0°.
Read the MASTER'S / PILOT'S ORDER card. It shows the current order, present heading and a 12 s 'steady' counter.
Instructor card: set ship 'Speed' (2–18 kn) and 'Sea / yaw' (calm, moderate, rough) to match conditions.
Set 'Wind on port bow (weather helm)'. The autopilot builds up a steady rudder 'Bias', shown in Tuning Info.
Leave tuning values (RG, CR, Timer, Level, Phase, Bias, INF) alone: the unit is labelled 'NOTE: TUNING DO NOT TOUCH'.
Press '⚙' to open Brightness. Turn the knob to change brightness 10–100%. Press 'ACCEPT' to close.
Repeater dimming: click the 'DIM −' or 'DIM +' box on the repeater face.
Keyboard: Left/Right arrow turns the knob 1° (Shift = 10°). Enter = 'ACCEPT'.
Turn the mode selector to HAND by clicking the left half of the selector knob.
Steer with the HELM (follow-up): drag the wheel, or use '◀ 5° P', 'MIDSHIPS', 'S 5° ▶'.
Watch ORDER and ACTUAL on the rudder indicator. The rudder follows the wheel at about 2.5°/s.
Meet the swing early and return to 'MIDSHIPS' to steady. The order completes after 12 s steady.
Helm buttons only work in HAND. Otherwise the screen shows 'SELECTOR NOT IN HAND'.

sections.h: Change over HAND to AUTO and course changes
steps: Steady the ship on the required heading in HAND first.
Click the right half of the selector until AUTO is underlined. Screen shows STBY and 'SELECTOR AUTO — press TAKE OVER'.
Press 'TAKE OVER'. Mode becomes HDG and SET HEADING copies the present gyro heading.
To alter course press 'SET HDG'. The label changes to PRESET HEADING and the value blinks.
Turn the knob to the new heading: click left/right half = 1°, mouse wheel = 1°, Shift+wheel = 10°, or drag.
Press 'ACCEPT'. Screen shows 'NEW HEADING … ACCEPTED' and the autopilot applies rudder.
Accept within 30 s or the screen shows 'PRESET TIMEOUT — not accepted' and the old heading stays.
Monitor the turn: repeater card rotates, right panel shows RUDDER, ROT and the active rudder/ROT limit.
Track mode is not fitted on this training unit. Only HDG mode is available.

sections.h: PRESET turn limit (rudder limit or rate of turn)
steps: With the selector in AUTO press 'PRESET'. The panel shows PRESET TURN MODE.
Turn 10 steps at once (Shift+wheel or Shift+arrow) to switch between RUDDER LIMIT and RATE OF TURN.
Single knob steps change the selected value by 5: rudder limit 5–35°, rate of turn 5–90°/min.
Press 'ACCEPT'. Screen confirms 'TURN MODE: RUDDER LIMIT …' or 'RATE OF TURN …°/min'.
Then use 'SET HDG' → knob → 'ACCEPT' to make the turn at the preset limit.

sections.h: Change over AUTO to HAND and emergency steering
steps: Before traffic, restricted waters or close-quarters, click the left half of the selector to HAND.
Screen shows HAND STEERING. The wheel takes the present rudder angle; steer and steady by helm.
Emergency drill: turn the selector to OFF (centre). Screen shows EMERGENCY STEERING.
The STEERING GEAR ROOM LOCAL CONTROL (NFU) panel lights up with heading and rudder readouts.
Hold '◀ PORT' or 'STBD ▶' to move the rudder. Release and the rudder stays where it is.
Steer the ordered heading by NFU using the panel's gyro heading. (On board: orders passed by phone from the bridge.)
NFU buttons only work with the selector in OFF ('LOCAL CONTROL ONLY WITH SELECTOR IN OFF').
An active alarm shows a red '⚠ ALARM' box with text on the autopilot screen and the buzzer sounds.
Press '🔇' to silence. The alarm box stays until the cause clears.
'Gyro failure': repeater freezes, shows blinking GYRO FAIL. Alarm 'HEADING SENSOR FAIL (GYRO 1)'. Mode shows HDG FAIL and rudder goes midships.
On gyro failure: press '🔇', turn the selector to HAND and steer by hand. 'TAKE OVER' is refused.
(On board) steer by magnetic compass and inform the Master. Click 'Gyro failure' again to restore the gyro.
'Steering gear failure (rudder stuck)': rudder stops moving. In HDG mode, 20 s off course by more than 8° raises 'OFF HEADING ALARM'.
On steering failure: press '🔇', report to the Master. (On board) change over steering pumps/systems. Click the button again to clear.
Brief the relieving officer: steering mode, set heading, turn mode and limit, rudder bias and any active alarms.
Confirm the repeater, GYRO 1 HEADING and order card agree before handing over.
Leave the selector in the mode ordered by the Master. Use HAND for pilotage.
Pause with '❚❚' or reset with '↺ RESTART'. Restart also clears the exercise ticks.
(On board) record steering changes in the deck log and test manual steering after long autopilot use.

tips: 'SET HDG' works only in HDG mode. Press 'TAKE OVER' first.
A steady rudder angle on a steady heading usually means weather helm, not a fault.
Use the inner fine card of the repeater to see small heading changes early.
The order card waits for 12 s of steady heading before marking an order complete.
Complete the QUICK QUIZ and the TRAINING EXERCISES list to finish the module.

bnwas.title: BNWAS Panel

steps: Open the trainer. The panel starts with the Master's key in AUTO and the autopilot box ticked.
Choose speed '×1' in the header. '×10' and '×30' shorten waiting; '❚❚' pauses; '↺ RESTART' resets the panel.
Check the red display shows a MM:SS countdown of the dormant period with a blinking colon.
Check the DORMANT TIMER box under the panel and the TIME TO STAGE 1/2/3 boxes in the side card.
Press 'SET/TEST' briefly. Display shows 8888 with all dots, buttons light and the buzzer sounds for about 3 s.
If any segment, lamp or buzzer fails, report it. (On board) log the test.
Adjust panel brightness with '−' and '+' (dimmer, five levels).
Click the left or right half of the key lock to turn it: OFF, ON or AUTO.
The display shows OFF, On or Aut for 2 s, then the countdown. Turning the key restarts the timer.
AUTO: BNWAS is active only while the autopilot (heading/track control) is engaged.
ON: always active. Use it when steering by hand.
OFF: BNWAS inactive and the buttons go dark. Only on the Master's order.
Engage or disengage the autopilot with the 'Autopilot (heading / track control) engaged' box. In AUTO without autopilot the display shows Aut.

sections.h: Set dormant period and stage-3 delay
steps: With the key in ON or AUTO, hold 'SET/TEST' for 3 s. Display shows d and the dormant period in minutes.
Press '−' or '+' to set 3–12 minutes. Standing order value is 9 min.
Press 'SET/TEST' briefly to move to the stage-3 delay. Display alternates S3 and the value in seconds.
Press '−' or '+' in 10 s steps (90–180 s). Standing order value is 90 s.
Press 'RESET' to save and exit. The log shows 'settings saved'.
The panel ships at 12 min / 120 s. Set the Master's values at the start of the exercise.
Reset before the countdown reaches 00:00. Press 'RESET' briefly on the panel.
Other resets: '🚶 OOW moves at console (motion sensor)', 'Reset on bridge wing', 'Ack on radar/ECDIS'.
Motion sensor resets need 'Motion sensors' set to 'fitted — reset on movement'. While the OOW is active it may reset on its own.
When the dormant period ends, stage 1 visual starts and 'RESET' flashes. Reset within 15 s, before the audible alarm.
Stage 1 visual: display alternates AL1 and time to next stage; 'RESET' flashes.
After 15 s: stage 1 audible on the bridge. After 30 s: stage 2 to Master and back-up officer cabins (AL2).
After the stage-3 delay: stage 3 to all crew (AL3). The four stage boxes in the side card light in turn.
To see the full sequence press '😴 OOW incapacitated (no activity)'. The timer jumps to 20 s before stage 1.
Reset from the bridge with 'RESET'. Record observed times in ALARM SEQUENCE OBSERVED, then 'CHECK'.
OOW needs help: hold 'RESET' for 3 s. Display blinks EC and stages 2 and 3 sound at once.
Cancel the emergency call by pressing 'RESET' briefly from the bridge.
'🆘 OOW needs help' marks the OOW as needing assistance for the emergency-call exercise.
Untick the autopilot box. In AUTO the BNWAS stops ('AUTO — waiting for autopilot').
Turn the key to ON at once so the BNWAS stays active while steering by hand.
When autopilot is re-engaged, return the key to AUTO as the standing order requires.
Hand over with the key in the mode set by the Master's standing order and the dormant period checked.
Do a 'SET/TEST' with the relieving officer and reset the timer before leaving the console.
Key to OFF only on the Master's order (e.g. in port). Display then shows OFF.
Pause with '❚❚' or start again with '↺ RESTART'.

tips: A stage-2 alarm will be investigated. Always reset during stage 1.
Settings cannot be opened with the key in OFF.
While in the settings menu the BNWAS timer is held at zero.
Use '×1' speed when timing the stages for the observation exercise.
The side log shows every reset, key change, stage and setting change with time.

vdr.title: VDR Remote Alarm Panel

steps: Open the trainer. The VDR is already recording on main power; the clock shows UTC.
Choose speed '×1'. '×10' and '×60' run faster, '❚❚' pauses, '↺ RESTART' resets the panel.
Read the status line in INSTRUCTOR · EVENTS: 'Recording: ON (main power)' and the list of active errors.
Note the panel at start: display shows 042 and the ERROR LED is steady (Radar 2 S-band fault already acknowledged).
Press 'TEST'. Display shows 888, SAVE, NORMAL and ERROR LEDs light and the buzzer sounds.
Report any dead segment, LED or buzzer. (On board) record the daily test in the log.
Night watch: press DIMMER '−' to the lowest level, then '+' back to normal.
Normal state: green NORMAL LED on, no error code, no buzzer.
An error shows a 3-digit code, the ERROR LED and buzzer. Several errors cycle on the display every 2 s.
Look up each code in the ERROR CODE TABLE card.
In ERROR REPORT enter the code in 'Code shown', pick the 'Faulty item', then press 'LOG IT'.
A correct entry appears in the log book list. A wrong code or item is rejected with the reason.
Inform the Master / ETO of every error. (On board) record it in the log book.
Press 'ACK' to silence the buzzer. The ERROR LED changes from flashing to steady.
The code stays on the display and ERROR stays lit until the fault is cleared.
A new fault restarts the buzzer and flashing LED. Press 'ACK' again and log the new code.
'Main power failure': code 001. VDR continues on the reserve battery; status shows minutes left (about 2 h).
Press 'ACK', log 001, inform Master / ETO. (On board) restore main power before the battery runs out.
If the battery runs out, code 002 appears and status shows 'STOPPED — battery exhausted'.
'Capsule fault': code 010, fixed capsule no connection. Press 'ACK', log it, report it.
Click any item in RECORDED DATA SOURCES to fail or restore it. Treat each new code the same way.
'Restore all' clears every fault and returns main power.
'⚠ COLLISION (incident)' starts the incident; the Master orders the data saved. Do not switch the VDR off.
Click '▲ lift cover' to open the cover over 'OPEN AFTER INCIDENT'.
Press and hold 'OPEN AFTER INCIDENT' about 3 s until the SAVE LED blinks. Releasing early cancels the save.
While saving, dashes run across the display. When done it shows End and the SAVE LED stays lit.
Log the UTC time of the incident and the save. The log shows 'incident data saved (last 12 h protected)'.
Click '▲ lift cover' again to close the cover.
Saving is impossible once the reserve battery is exhausted.
(On board) inform company/DPA and flag state; hand data only to the investigating authority.
Never switch the VDR off at sea or after an incident.
Hand over: active error codes, whether acknowledged and logged, power source, and any incident saves.
Confirm NORMAL LED, or list the faults still showing, before leaving the bridge.
Pause with '❚❚' or start again with '↺ RESTART'.

tips: 'ACK' silences only; it does not clear a fault.
With several errors, watch one full cycle of the display to read every code.
Use the 'AFTER AN INCIDENT' card to practise the correct order of actions.
Codes are training values. Use your own VDR manual on board.

gvm.title: Gyro vs Magnetic Compass

steps: Open the trainer. Speed '×1'; '×10' speeds up turns; '❚❚' pauses; '↺ RESTART' clears the book and faults.
Check the GYRO REPEATER and its GYRO HEADING digital readout agree.
Check the STEERING (MAGNETIC) COMPASS card. Read it by eye at the red lubber line.
Read INFORMATION FOR THE WATCH: gyro error 1.0° High, variation 0°30'W.
Set sea state in INSTRUCTOR 'Sea' (calm, moderate, rough). Rougher sea makes the magnetic card swing more.
Alter course with HELM ORDER buttons '◀ 30°', '◀ 10°', '◀ 1°', '1° ▶', '10° ▶', '30° ▶'.
The ordered heading shows between the buttons. Wait until the ship and magnetic card are steady.
With the ship steady, read the gyro heading to 0.1°. Enter it under 'Gyro'.
Enter the gyro error under 'G.err' with H or L, for example 1.0H.
Work out True: High → subtract from gyro, Low → add. Enter under 'True'.
Read the magnetic compass at the lubber line. Enter it under 'Mag C'.
Compass error = True − Compass. Enter under 'C.err' with E or W (E if True is greater).
Deviation = Compass error − Variation (0.5W). Enter under 'Dev' with E or W.
Press 'LOG'. If not steady, the tool says wait. Wrong boxes are listed with the correct working.
A correct entry is added to the COMPASS ERROR BOOK with time.
The result compares your deviation with the DEVIATION CARD for that compass heading.
Difference over 2° is flagged ⚠ in the book: check for magnetic objects, recheck, inform the Master, log it.
Log comparisons on at least 4 headings 30° or more apart.
'Magnetic object left near compass': deviation changes and no longer agrees with the card.
Log a comparison, note the ⚠ flag, look for and remove the object, recheck and report to the Master.
Click the button again to remove the object.
'Gyro wander (error grows)': gyro error slowly increases to as much as 4°. The posted 1.0° High is no longer valid.
Logs with the old error will fail. (On board) find a new gyro error by azimuth or transit and inform the Master.
Click the button again to stop the wander.
Hand over the latest gyro error, compass error and deviation from the book.
Report any flagged entry or suspected fault to the relieving officer and the Master.
Pause with '❚❚' or clear everything with '↺ RESTART'.

tips: Compare only on a steady heading; the magnetic card lags and swings in a turn.
Do a comparison every watch and after every major course alteration.
Enter errors with letters: H/L for gyro error, E/W for compass error and deviation.
The INSTRUCTOR line shows the true values for checking.

mag.title: Magnetic Compass & Deviation

steps: Open the trainer. Clock starts at 07:30 LT. Speed '×1'; '×10' or '×60' moves the sun faster; '↺ RESTART' resets.
Check COMPASS READINGS: 'COMPASS HEADING (lubber line)' and 'AZIMUTH CIRCLE · COMPASS BEARING'.
Check the true heading in SHIP · HELM · GYRO. Gyro error here is zero.
Note the variation from the chart: 0°30'W. Set 'Roll' (calm, slight, moderate).
After dusk press '💡 Binnacle light' so the card can be read.
Choose Method 'Gyro comparison (heading)'.
Wait for the card to settle. Read the compass heading at the lubber line; enter in 'Compass reading'.
Enter the gyro true heading in 'True'.
Comp. error = True − Compass; enter with E or W, e.g. 1.5W.
Deviation = Compass error − Variation; enter with E or W. Press 'CHECK'.
The result marks each box ✔ or ✘ and shows the full working.
Choose Method 'Sun azimuth (azimuth circle)'. The info line gives the sun's true azimuth when it is high enough.
Drag the azimuth circle on the compass picture until the SIGHT line points at the sun. Mouse wheel = 0.2°, Shift = ×10.
Read 'AZIMUTH CIRCLE · COMPASS BEARING'. Enter it as the compass reading.
Enter the true azimuth, compass error and deviation, then press 'CHECK'.
If the circle is off the sun the result says 'sight it first'.
Choose Method 'Transit — leading lights'. True bearing is 158.0°T from the chart.
Sight the LDG LTS with the azimuth circle and read the compass bearing.
Enter compass reading, True 158.0, compass error and deviation. Press 'CHECK'.
Press '⟳ SWING SHIP (auto-steer 8 headings)'. The ship steadies on 000°C, 045°C … 315°C in turn.
On each heading, when the card settles, press '● RECORD this heading'.
If the card is still moving the button shows 'wait — card swinging'.
The DEVIATION LOG lists ship's head, gyro true, variation, magnetic and deviation.
Helm buttons '−10', '−1', '+1', '+10' steer by hand and stop the automatic swing.
Compare the log with the posted DEVIATION CARD.
Watch the DEVIATION CURVE (live). 'max dev' turns green at 2° or less.
Fore & aft magnets (B): '−' / '+' reduce the deviation on east–west headings.
Athwartship magnets (C): '−' / '+' reduce the deviation on north–south headings.
Quadrantal spheres (D): '◀' / '▶' move them from 'out' to 'in' to reduce intercardinal deviation.
Flinders bar: '−' / '+' in 3-inch steps; it changes with latitude.
Adjust until max deviation is 2° or less, then swing and record again. (On board) adjusting is done by a qualified compass adjuster.
Hand over the latest compass error, deviation on the present heading and any corrector changes.
Switch the binnacle light as needed for the next watch.
Pause with '❚❚' or reset with '↺ RESTART'.

tips: Only read the compass when the card has settled.
Compass least, error east; compass best, error west.
Deviation changes with the ship's heading; always state the heading it applies to.
This trainer has no failure buttons; practise by changing correctors and heading.

gyroerr.title: Gyro Error

steps: Open the trainer. A random gyro error is set; the header shows UTC and LT.
Check the bridge-wing GYRO REPEATER card, lubber line and SHIP'S HEAD (GYRO) readout.
Read SHIP & OBSERVATION DATA: DR position, LT = UTC + 8, Sun Dec S 3°05.6', Ldg Lts 087.0°T.
Choose a method tab: 'A · TRANSIT', 'B · SUN AZIMUTH', 'C · AMPLITUDE', 'D · APPLY THE ERROR' or 'E · BLANK PAPER'.
Follow the step player. Use '💡 HINT' for help, '◀ BACK' and 'NEXT ▶' to move between steps.
Turn the circle with AZIMUTH buttons '⟲ 5°', '⟲ 1°', '⟲ 0.2°', '0.2° ⟳', '1° ⟳', '5° ⟳'.
Or drag the view, drag the brass ring on the repeater, or use the mouse wheel for 0.1°.
Before any sun sight press 'Dark glass: off' to switch it ON. Without it the view shows a glare warning.
Put the object on the hairline and press '⏱ MARK'. The time is recorded to the second.
A good MARK shows ✔. A bad one says why: off the hairline, no dark glass, or wrong moment.
After a good MARK the circle is locked. Read the gyro card in the prism strip below the view.
Turn the circle towards the leading lights, about 085–090° on the card.
Keep the hairline on the front light as the ship yaws. Use 0.2° steps or the wheel.
Press '⏱ MARK' the moment the rear light is exactly above the front light.
Missed it? Press '↺ RUN AGAIN'. The run also restarts if the ship passes the line.
Read the prism to 0.1° and enter it in 'Gyro bearing read in the prism', then 'CHECK'.
Complete the worksheet: G, True 087.0, G − T, error and HIGH/LOW. Press '✔ CHECK WORKSHEET'.

sections.h: B · Sun azimuth and C · Amplitude
steps: Sun azimuth: dark glass ON, turn to the sun, centre it on the hairline, press '⏱ MARK'.
Read the prism, enter the gyro bearing and press 'CHECK'.
Fill the worksheet line by line: Lat, Dec, LHA, trig values, denominator, tan Z, Z, Zn, error, HIGH/LOW.
Amplitude: time runs ×8. Dark glass ON, follow the rising sun on the hairline.
Press '⏱ MARK' when the lower limb is about half a diameter above the horizon.
Too early or late is rejected. Use '↺ RUN AGAIN' to repeat the sunrise.
Complete the amplitude worksheet: sin A, A, name E … S, Zn, error. Press '✔ CHECK WORKSHEET'.
Each line has '💡' (where the value comes from) and '👁' (show answer, marked as helped).
A correct worksheet logs time, method, gyro, true and error (H/L) in the GYRO ERROR BOOK.
If your MARK was more than 0.4° off, a warning tells you to be more careful.
Open 'D · APPLY THE ERROR' after logging at least one error with A, B or C.
Copy your error from the book. True → Gyro: HIGH add, LOW subtract. Find the gyro course for 135.0°T.
Gyro → True: HIGH subtract, LOW add. Convert lighthouse bearing 042.5°G to true for plotting.
Press '✔ CHECK WORKSHEET'. The result gives the course to steer and the true bearing.
Pick a problem type: 'Transit (lights in line)', 'Sun azimuth', 'Moon azimuth' or 'Sun amplitude'.
Read the GIVEN and the ALMANAC EXTRACT. Fill each line, choosing names from the drop-downs.
Formats: angles '123 45.6', time '22 24 18'. Use the rough-work box for working.
Press '✔ CHECK PAPER'. Score shows; fix the first wrong line, using '💡' if needed.
Press '📄 NEW PROBLEM' for another paper. Solve all four types to complete the task.
Hand over the latest gyro error from the GYRO ERROR BOOK, with method and time.
Check the error every watch and after large course alterations. (On board) record it in the compass error book.
Press '🎲 NEW ERROR' to start over with a new error. This clears the book, marks and progress.

tips: Never look at the sun without the dark glass.
Gyro error = Gyro − True. Gyro more than True is HIGH.
A transit is the quickest check of gyro error in pilotage waters.
Errors from different methods should agree within about 0.5°.
This trainer has no failure buttons or speed controls; amplitude runs at ×8 automatically.

radar.title: Radar / ARPA

steps: (On board) Check the scanner is clear of people, then switch on and wait out the magnetron warm-up before TRANSMIT.
The simulator opens already transmitting: the bottom-left button reads "STANDBY" while the radar is running.
Pick a situation under PRACTICE SITUATIONS (start with No. 1); it loads paused and the button changes to "TRANSMIT".
Read the brief, then press "TRANSMIT" to run the exercise. Press "STANDBY" any time to freeze it.
Check NAV DATA on the left: HDG, STW (log), SOG/COG (GPS), current set and drift.
Choose the range with the RANGE selector (3, 6, 12 or 24 NM) under MEASUREMENT / GUARD ZONE.
Set GAIN until a light speckle of background noise just shows.
Raise A/C SEA until the sea clutter around own ship is thinned, without losing small close targets.
Use A/C RAIN to break up rain echoes; reduce it again when the rain has passed.
Fine-tune in MENU → ECHO PROCESSING: INTERFERENCE REJ., ECHO STRETCH, ECHO AVERAGE and PULSE LENGTH.
Use "X-BAND" / "S-BAND" to switch band, and "RINGS 6" to cycle range rings 6, 4, 8 or off.
Press "NORTH UP" to cycle NORTH UP, COURSE UP and HEAD UP (also MENU → ORIENTATION).
In COURSE UP, press "RESET C-UP TO HEADING" in MENU after a course change.
Press "GROUND STAB" / "SEA STAB" to choose the true-vector reference; use SEA STAB for open-sea collision avoidance.
Press "REL VECTOR" / "TRUE VECTOR" to switch vector mode; "TRAILS ON" toggles relative trails.
Press "OFF CENTRE", then click the PPI where own ship should sit; press again to re-centre.
Use "FIT", "LARGE", "MAX" or "FULL SCREEN" for screen size; "BRIDGE VIEW" shows the 3D lookout view.
Press "EBL 1 OFF" to switch the bearing line on, then drag the EBL 1 slider onto the echo.
Press "VRM 1 OFF" to switch the range ring on, then drag the VRM 1 slider to touch the echo.
Read EBL and VRM values in the top-right readout of the PPI.
Hover the cursor over any point to read BRG, RNG and LAT/LON in CURSOR POSITION.
Take repeated EBL bearings: a steady bearing with closing range means risk of collision.
Press "PI SETUP" (or MENU → PARALLEL INDEX) and choose INDIVIDUAL LINES or EQUAL SPACING (PAIRS).
For each line tick PI 1–3, enter BRG °T (planned track), DIST NM, SIDE (STBD/PORT) and TYPE (INDEX or LIMIT).
Press "PI OFF" / "PI ON" on the main panel to show or hide the lines.
Under way, keep the fixed echo sliding along the INDEX line; if it drifts off, alter course to bring it back.
A "PI LIMIT" alert shows if the echo crosses a LIMIT line.
Practise with MENU → "PI · TSS STRAIT · ISLANDS & SET (LOADS NOW)".
Click an echo on the PPI to select it; the message reads "selected. Press ACQUIRE TARGET".
Press "ACQUIRE TARGET". Up to two targets can be tracked (TARGET INFO · MAX 2).
Wait for the vector to settle, then read BRG, RNG, COG, SOG, TC*/STW*, CPA and TCPA in TARGET INFO.
Set CPA LIMIT NM and TCPA LIMIT MIN in MENU → TARGET / ARPA.
Press "ACQUIRE TARGET" again on a selected tracked target to cancel tracking.
Press "ASSESS SITUATION" to pause and see the COLREG judgement for every ship; "CLOSE · RESUME" continues.
Use the COLREG COACH: pick the target under ANALYSE TARGET and read aspect, bearing trend and CPA/TCPA.
Use the "WHAT IF…? · FAST-TIME PREDICTION" table as a trial manoeuvre: it shows CPA and verdict for each option.
To alter course, type the course in SET COURSE and press "STEER", or use P10, P1, S1, S10.
Choose "SHORTEST", "VIA PORT" or "VIA STBD"; "STEADY · CANCEL TURN" stops a turn.
Change speed with "◀ ASTERN" / "AHEAD ▶" or the ORDERED STW slider. Orders execute only while transmitting.
Press "GUARD ON" to toggle the guard zone; set ranges with the GZ INNER and GZ OUTER sliders.
Press "SET GUARD", then drag on the PPI from one corner to the opposite corner to draw the zone.
Or set GUARD START ° REL, GUARD END ° REL and ARC WIDTH in MENU → GUARD ZONE.
Press "ENABLE AUDIO" once so alarms can sound.
Watch the ALERTS strip: CPA / TCPA, GZ1 TARGET, PI LIMIT, COLLISION IMMINENT.
Press "ALARM ACK" for guard-zone alarms and "ACK" on the COLLISION IMMINENT banner, then act.
Run MENU → PERFORMANCE MONITOR: choose TEST CONDITION and press "START PERFORMANCE TEST" while transmitting.
Check OPERATING HOURS for magnetron total and TX time used.
Press "SART EX" for the SART exercise; use EBL/VRM, then "REPORT SART POSITION (EBL/VRM)".
Open "SEPARATE LESSON · SEA STAB INPUT ERRORS" in MENU to see how wrong heading or speed inputs affect vectors.
Cancel ARPA targets that are no longer needed.
Press "STANDBY"; the button changes to "TRANSMIT" and the picture stops updating.
Press "RESET" to restore the last applied scenario if you want to repeat it.
(On board) Leave the radar in STANDBY if needed again soon; otherwise switch off at the main switch.

tips: Scenarios always load paused: read the brief, then press "TRANSMIT".
Orders from helm and telegraph only take effect while transmitting.
Unchanged CPA after switching stabilisation is normal: relative vectors and CPA/TCPA use measured relative motion.
Press Esc to close the radar MENU.
"EASY WORDS: OFF" switches the briefs and coach to simpler English.

ecdis.title: ECDIS (Manila – Cebu)

steps: Open the simulator: the self test ("ECDIS TRAINING SYSTEM · SELF TEST") loads the presentation library, ENC cells and sensors.
Wait for "System ready." or press "SKIP ▸". Check the green POWER LED on the console bar.
Check the bottom status bar: GPS1, GYRO1, LOG1 and AIS should show green.
Open NAVI ▸ Sensor status: confirm position, heading, speed, depth and AIS show OK.
Compare HDG/STW with COG/SOG on the right panel to see set and drift.
Click the ENC update item on the status bar (or left-bar "ENC UPD") to open ENC UPDATE STATUS.
Every cell must show UP TO DATE and permits must be valid; note any NOT UP TO DATE (SSE 27) cells.
Press left-bar "SAFETY" (or the "SET" button beside SAFETY PARAMETERS).
In the SAFETY DEPTH CALCULATOR enter draft, Cb, speed, water type, UKC policy and tide; press "USE RESULT → SAFETY DEPTH & CONTOUR".
Check safety contour, safety depth, shallow and deep contours.
Set look-ahead time and width, default XTD, CPA/TCPA limits and wheel-over warning.
Press "APPLY & RECHECK ROUTE". Confirm values in SAFETY PARAMETERS and the status bar (SC, SD, LA).
Press left-bar "DISP" to set display category: use STANDARD; never navigate on BASE.
Choose colour palette DAY, DUSK or NIGHT; left-bar "DAY" or the "DAY NIGHT" key also cycles it.
Choose 4 or 2 depth shades and the shallow water pattern.
Press "PRES LIB" to compare PAPER CHART and SIMPLIFIED symbols, SYMBOLIZED and PLAIN boundaries.
Use the chart quick buttons: "CAT: STANDARD", "4 SHADES", "SYM: PAPER", "BND: SYMBOLIZED", "IALA: B", "FOLLOW SHIP".
Press "↺ RESET TO IMO STANDARD DISPLAY" to return to the standard display. Adjust brightness with "BRILL −" / "BRILL +".

sections.h: ENC update and permits by USB
steps: In ENC UPDATE STATUS press "⬇ UPDATE VIA USB · STEP BY STEP".
Step 1: choose "A · ONLINE CHART SERVICE" ("SYNCHRONISE", then "EXPORT TO USB") or "B · E-MAIL TO THE MASTER" ("SAVE ATTACHMENTS TO USB").
Step 2: press "SCAN USB" on the standalone PC, then "NEXT ▸ INSERT IN ECDIS".
Step 3: press "INSERT USB NOW" or click the console USB port.
Step 4: press "INSTALL PERMITS (PERMIT.TXT)" first.
Step 5: press "IMPORT ENC UPDATES", then "VIEW CHANGES ON CHART" to see new lights, buoys and dangers.
Step 6: press "VERIFY · ENC UPDATE STATUS", check the "ENC UPDATE LOG", then "EJECT USB". Check AIO with "AIO / T&P NOTICES".
Press left-bar "PLAN" (or PLAN ▸ Create new route). Left-click to drop WPT 01, 02, 03…
Press-hold and drag to pan without adding waypoints; right-click a leg to insert, or a waypoint to edit, move or delete.
Double-click the last waypoint or press "✓ END ROUTE"; "↶ UNDO LAST" removes the last point.
Press "☰ TABLE" or left-bar "ROUTE" to edit names, XTD and speeds in the route table.
Save the route ("SAVE ROUTE"). For practice use PLAN ▸ Load sample route: it has a hidden problem.
Press left-bar "CHECK" (or "✓ CHECK ROUTE").
Red alarms (land, safety contour, hazards) must be fixed: use "LOCATE", then move or insert waypoints.
Review every yellow caution, then press "ACCEPT ALL CAUTIONS".
Save and check again after every change, including after ENC updates.
Press "APEM" for the passage plan ("PASSAGE PLAN (APEM)") and "MASTER APPROVAL"; "PRINT / SAVE PDF" if needed.
Press left-bar "VOYAGE": select the route and press "NEXT ▸".
Confirm the route is saved and checked, then "NEXT ▸"; set start position, departure time and simulation speed.
Press "▶ START VOYAGE": the route activates, TRACK steering engages and monitoring starts.
Watch ROUTE MONITORING: active leg, BRG/DIST, XTE, XTD limit, next course, TTG/ETA.
Use "HDG" or "TRACK", −10°/−1°/+1°/+10°, the SPD slider and SIM × (❚❚, 1, 4, 10, 30, 60).
Use "ERBL", "DIVIDER", "AIS", "RADAR" overlay and "WPT ETA / REQ. SPEED" as needed.
Watch the alert banner and the ALARMS panel on the right.
Read each alarm, then press "ACK ALL" or the console "ALARM ACK" key; "BUZZER STOP" silences the buzzer.
Act on the cause: alter course, check depth, or check the failed sensor.
For man overboard press "MOB" (left bar or red console key) to mark the position.
Instructors can inject sensor failures in NAVI ▸ Sensor status.
Press left-bar "VIDEO" (or OTHERS ▸ Video lessons) to open the ECDIS video lessons.
Watch Part 1 ENC updates, Part 2 Safety settings, Part 3 Presentation library and Part 4 Route planning.
Press "TRAINING EXERCISES" or "OPEN EXERCISES" and repeat each step yourself.
Review events with left-bar "LOG".

sections.h: End of voyage and shut down
steps: Press "■ STOP VOYAGE" in VOYAGE (or left-bar "MONITOR") to stop route monitoring; steering returns to HDG.
Check the event log and ENC update log are complete.
Make sure the USB stick has been ejected.
Select OTHERS ▸ "Power OFF / self test": the simulator restarts its self test.
(On board) Shut down through the manufacturer's menu, never by cutting power.

tips: Never navigate on BASE display: use STANDARD as a minimum.
Install permits before importing updates, or the import is refused.
Any ENC update clears the route check: check the route again.
Three route cells start NOT UP TO DATE; their missing dangers do not show until you update.
Left-bar "CATZOC" and "AIO" toggle data-quality and T&P notice overlays.

sextant.title: Sextant

steps: Choose "📘 GUIDED TUTORIAL" to be led step by step, or "✋ FREE PRACTICE" to work alone.
Use "NEXT ▶", "◀ BACK" and "💡 HINT" in the step player under the sextant.
Click each part of the sextant to learn its name: index mirror, horizon mirror, drum, clamp.
"🎲 NEW SEXTANT" gives a sextant with new errors and restarts the tutorial.
Press VIEW "INTO INDEX MIRROR" to look obliquely into the index mirror.
Compare the arc seen directly with its reflection: they must form one continuous line.
If there is a step, turn "Index mirror ⟲" / "⟳" until the line is continuous.
You can also click the screw (shift-click reverses) or scroll over it.
Press VIEW "HORIZON (IE / side)".
Press "✊ RELEASE CLAMP", bring the arm near 0° with −5°/−1°, lock the clamp and line up the horizons with the drum.
Press "⤾ TILT": if the horizons split, there is side error.
Turn "H.mirror side ⟲" / "⟳" until the horizons stay in line when tilted.
Hold the sextant upright on the HORIZON view.
Turn the drum (−5' to +5', ±0.2') until direct and reflected horizons form one straight line.
Read the error from the magnified arc and drum: index above 0 = ON the arc; below 0 = OFF (60' − drum).
Enter the value, choose ON the arc or OFF the arc, and press "RECORD IE".
Small errors (under 3') are recorded, not removed. Larger ones can be reduced with "H.mirror index ⟲" / "⟳".
Press VIEW "SUN". Never look at the sun without shades.
Press "Index shades" to add shades; add "Horizon shade" if the sea glitters.
Press "✊ RELEASE CLAMP" and bring the sun down with +5°/+1° until it nears the horizon.
Lock the clamp and turn the drum until the lower limb just touches the horizon.
Press "↔ ROCK": at the bottom of the swing the limb should just kiss the horizon.
The sun keeps rising: keep making small + drum corrections, then press "⏱ MARK" at contact.
Do not touch the sextant; use the magnifier at bottom right.
Degrees: the arc graduation just right of the index mark.
Minutes: the drum figure at its index line.
Tenths: the vernier line that meets a drum line.
Check against the ARC, DRUM and SEXTANT ALT read-outs, enter Hs and press "CHECK READING".

sections.h: Applying index error and reducing the sight
steps: In REDUCE THE SIGHT enter your Hs from your MARK.
Enter index error: ON the arc is subtracted (−), OFF the arc is added (+).
Enter dip for 18 m height of eye (1.76′ × √HE, always subtract).
Find the Sun lower-limb total correction from the table, interpolating for apparent altitude.
Enter Ho and press "CHECK".
Complete the TRAINING EXERCISES card and the QUICK QUIZ, then press "SUBMIT".
(On board) Remove shades, return the arm to zero, clamp it and stow the sextant in its box.

tips: Always correct errors in this order: perpendicularity, side error, index error.
"On is off, off is on": subtract IE on the arc, add IE off the arc.
Use 0.2' drum steps for the final contact.
If a MARK was poor, adjust the drum again and MARK again.

plotting.title: Radar Plotting Sheet

steps: "GUIDED DEMO" walks a scenario step by step on the sheet.
"LESSON · LEARN e-r-m" explains the plotting letters and triangle.
"PRACTICE · YOU PLOT" makes you plot and measure yourself.
"MY SCENARIO · STEP BY STEP" lets a trainer enter their own observations and coaches the student.
"e-r-m LABELS: ON" shows the letters; "EASY WORDS: OFF" switches to simpler English.
Pick a scenario from SCENARIOS on the left.
Note own course, speed and sheet scale under OWN SHIP.
Read the target's bearings and ranges in RADAR OBSERVATIONS · TARGET (true bearings, north-up).
For your own data, open "INSTRUCTOR · CUSTOM EXERCISE", enter own ship and three observations, then press "PLOT THIS EXERCISE".
In MY SCENARIO press "✎ TRAINER SET-UP", fill in the observations (or "FILL EXAMPLE") and press "START ▶".
In the demo, step with "NEXT ▶" and "◀ PREV"; "SHOW ALL" reveals every step.
In practice, click each position on the sheet, or type BRG and RNG in the worksheet row and press "PLOT".
Join the first and last plots: this is the relative motion line (RML), r → m.
A third plot should fall on the RML; if not, the target has altered.
Plot own ship's run in the interval back from the first plot (own speed × interval ÷ 60): this gives W (e).
WO / er is own ship's vector; OA / rm is the relative motion.
Join W to the last plot: WA / em is the target's true vector.
Press "ZOOM TRIANGLE" to enlarge it; measure with "📏 DIVIDERS" on the distance scale.
Transfer the true vector through own ship to read the target's true course on the bearing ring.
Extend the RML past own ship.
CPA is the perpendicular distance from own ship to the extended RML.
Relative speed = RML distance between plots × 60 ÷ minutes.
TCPA = distance from last plot to CPA point ÷ relative speed × 60.
Enter CPA, TCPA, true course, speed and aspect in STUDENT CHECK and press "CHECK MY ANSWERS".
In the GUIDED DEMO, step to "OWN SHIP'S ACTION" to see the new own vector and new RML.
Read the New RML, relative speed and New CPA in RESULTS.
In MY SCENARIO, press "NEXT: WHAT SHOULD I DO? ▶" after the triangle to choose the situation and action.
In a custom exercise, enter "Action at +min" and "New course / speed" (e.g. 060/12) before plotting.
Use "SHOW ME" or "SHOW ME THIS TASK" if stuck.
Press "RESET", "START AGAIN" or "RESTART PRACTICE" to repeat.
Try every scenario until your paper answers match the checks.

tips: Own vector + relative vector = target's true vector (WO + OA = WA, er + rm = em).
Work the answer on paper first, then check it here.
If W falls on the last plot, the target is stopped.
Bearings are true and the sheet is north-up, sea-stabilised.

wefax.title: Weather Fax Receiver

steps: Press the "POWER" rocker below the display; the LCD lights up.
Check paper is loaded; the printer cover opens to load paper.
Press "DIM" for night watch if the panel is too bright.
Check the STATION SCHEDULE card for product times (UTC) and assigned frequencies CH01–CH04.
Step channels with "2" (▲) / "8" (▼), or press "CH", a number 1–4 and "E".
Watch the TUNE bar: choose the channel with all three segments lit.
Daytime or long distance: higher frequency. Night: lower frequency.
To enter a frequency by hand press "FRQ", type the kHz ("REV" = decimal point), then "E".
Press "SPD" until AUTO and "IOC" until AUTO.
The recorder waits for the start signal, phases for 30 s, prints, and stops by itself.
Use "⏭ NEXT BROADCAST" to jump to just before the next transmission; speed up time with the buttons at the top.
Watch the TIMER and RCD lights.
Set "SPD" 120 and "IOC" 576, then press "RCD" during PHASING to start; "RCD" again to stop.
A slanted chart means wrong SPD; a stretched one means wrong IOC.
If the chart is split sideways, turn the "SYNC" knob until it is centred.
Satellite images use IOC 288; IOC AUTO recognises their start signal.
To set a timer: "PRG" → "1" → "E" → HHMM → ▲/▼ channel → "E".
To reprint from memory: "PRG" → "2" → ▲/▼ → "E".
To change print contrast: "PRG" → "3".
"C" clears or goes back one step.
Press "0" to feed paper past the tear bar.
Click the tear bar under the paper window to tear off the chart.
(On board) File the chart and brief the OOW and Master.

sections.h: Reading the chart and plotting own ship
steps: Press "🔍 OPEN CHART VIEWER" and choose a received SURFACE ANALYSIS (instructor: "📄 Sample analysis (instructor)").
Press "📖 START CHART READING" to open the questions.
Select "📍 Plot ship" and click your given latitude and longitude; use the grid and read-out.
Use "📏 Dividers" to measure bearing and distance; "✋ Look" to pan; "Fit", "100%", "150%" to zoom.
Answer pressure, wind, typhoon bearing and distance, semicircle, action and 24-h DR questions.
Use "💡 Hint" and "👁 Answer" if needed; press "✔ CHECK" for your score. "✕ CLOSE" exits.
Make sure no timer reception is pending if you want the set off.
Press the "POWER" rocker to OFF.
Press "↺ RESET" to start the trainer again from the beginning.

tips: Weather fax routine: check schedule, choose channel, set SPD and IOC to AUTO, tear off and brief.
On a general SSB receiver tune USB 1.9 kHz below the assigned frequency; this receiver applies the offset itself.
The TASKS card lists every skill to practise, with key sequences.
Instructors can inject "Paper end", "Signal fading (10 min)", "New weather scenario" and "+12 h (day/night)".

vhf.title: VHF DSC Radiotelephone

steps: Click the centre of the 'VOLUME/POWER' knob. The display shows 'SELF CHECK… ROM/RAM OK' and the radio starts on channel 16.
Check the channel display reads 16 'DISTRESS/CALL' and the line 'MANUAL ACK | AUTO CH:CH16'.
Set volume: click the left or right side of 'VOLUME/POWER', or use the mouse wheel on it (1 to 9).
Set 'SQUELCH' (wheel or left/right click). At 1–2 the display shows 'SQL OPEN - NOISE'; raise it until the noise just disappears.
Check the 'Hi' power tag. Press '* ▲SHIFT' then '0 HI/LO' to switch to 'Lo' for close-range or bridge-to-bridge calls.
(On board) keep a continuous watch on channel 16 and DSC channel 70 while at sea.
Change channel by typing two digits on the keypad (e.g. '1' '3'), turning the 'CHANNEL' knob, or using the 'CHANGE CHANNEL' buttons.
Press 'CH16' at any time to return to channel 16.
For dual watch, first select a working channel (not 16), e.g. 13.
Press '* ▲SHIFT' then '9 DW'. The display shows 'DW' and '+16' beside the channel number.
Press 'SHIFT' + '9 DW' again to stop dual watch. 'SHIFT' + '8 SCAN' starts or stops channel scanning.
Channel 70 is DSC only: the radio refuses voice on it, and 15/17 are limited to 1 W.
Daily test (as the placard): press '* ▲SHIFT' then '3 TEST'.
Wait for 'SELF TEST' to show ROM, RAM, LCD, KEY, TX, RX and 'DSC CH70 RX OK', then 'TEST COMPLETED'.
Check the position and UTC on the main screen ('LAT:' / 'LON:' lines with UTC time).
Or press 'MENU', select 'POSITION' with the knob and press 'ENT' to see the GPS position and time.
DSC test call: press 'CALL/MSG'; in 'COMPOSE DSC CALL' set 'TYPE' to 'TEST' (ENT, knob, ENT).
Select 'STATION ID', press 'ENT', key in 005480001, press 'ENT', then press 'CALL/MSG' to send.
Wait for 'TEST ACK RCVD' from the coast station. Press 'CANCEL' or 'ENT' to close.
Undesignated: leave the nature as set ('Undesignated' by default) and go straight to the DISTRESS button.
Designated: press 'MENU', select 'DISTRESS MSG EDIT', turn the knob to the nature (e.g. 'Fire / explosion') and press 'ENT'.
Click the transparent cover to lift it, then press and hold 'DISTRESS' for 4 seconds until it lights steady.
The display shows 'DISTRESS ALERT CH70', then 'DISTRESS SENT … Waiting for ACK… Listening CH16'.
When 'DISTRESS ACK' arrives, press 'CANCEL' to stop the alarm.
Click the handset to lift it, build the MAYDAY in the 'HANDSET — RADIOTELEPHONY' panel, check CH16, and hold 'PTT' to send.
Instructor button 'VHF DSC distress (vicinity)' gives 'DISTRESS RCVD' with an alarm.
Press 'CANCEL' to stop the alarm. Do NOT press '5 ACK' — the radio warns against DSC acknowledgement.
Stay on CH16 and listen. Give the coast station time to acknowledge (about 25 s in this simulator).
If 'Coast station ACK of that distress' is pressed, 'DISTRESS ACK' appears: keep watch on CH16, no action needed.
If no coast station acknowledges and the ship is near, acknowledge by RT on CH16 (RECEIVED MAYDAY format) with the handset.
This VHF has no DSC relay option. (On board) inform the coast station or RCC by RT or other means.
Press 'CALL/MSG'. Set 'TYPE' to 'INDIVIDUAL', 'STATION ID' to 548777222, 'CATEGORY' to 'ROUTINE'.
Set 'WORK CH' to an intership channel (06, 08, 72, 77). For the coast station 005480001 use 24, 26, 27, 12 or 14.
Press 'CALL/MSG' to send. When 'ACK RCVD … ABLE TO COMPLY' shows, press 'ENT' to accept the working channel.
Lift the handset, build the radio check message and hold 'PTT' on the working channel.
Incoming DSC call ('DSC individual call (ch request)'): press 'ENT' to accept; the radio changes to channel 08.
Voice call on CH16 ('Ship calls you on CH16'): answer on 16, agree channel 72, type '7' '2', then call again.
SECURITE: 'CALL/MSG', 'TYPE' 'ALL SHIPS', 'CATEGORY' 'SAFETY', send, then announce on CH16 by handset.
Do not switch the radio off.
Press 'MENU', select 'DISTRESS CANCEL (DSC)' and press 'ENT'. The display shows 'DSC cancel sent. Now cancel by RT on CH16'.
Lift the handset and build 'ALL STATIONS' ×3, 'THIS IS', name/call sign/MMSI, position, 'CANCEL MY DISTRESS ALERT OF…', '= MASTER…', 'OUT'.
Check CH16 is selected and hold 'PTT' to transmit. A green '✔ Correct message transmitted' confirms it.
(On board) record the false alert and cancellation in the GMDSS radio log.
Press '# ▼LOG' or 'FILE' to view the log: self tests and sent calls with UTC times.
Scroll with the knob or '*'/'#', and press 'CANCEL' to close.
(On board) copy the entries into the GMDSS radio logbook.
Put the handset back on hook (click it).
Click the centre of 'VOLUME/POWER' to switch off. (On board) switch off only when allowed by the SMS.

tips: In menus and forms: turn the 'CHANNEL' knob to move, push its centre (or 'ENT') to select, 'CANCEL' to go back.
Mouse: wheel or click the left/right side of a knob to turn it; the PC keyboard arrows, Enter and Esc also work.
The 'TRAINING EXERCISES' list ticks each task as you complete it; '↺ RESET' starts again.
Instructor buttons only work with the radio switched on.
Messages by handset are built from the word chips in order; use '⟲ UNDO' or 'CLEAR' to fix mistakes.

mfhf.title: MF/HF DSC Radio

steps: The radio is already on when the page opens; '↺ RESET' restarts it. This simulator has no working power switch.
Check the RT screen: '2182.0', 'ANT TUNED', position and 'PWR MAIN 24V'.
If the screen shows 'DSC SCAN: OFF (watch stopped!)', press '6 SCAN'.
Push the knob centre on 'SCAN : ON/OFF' to set it ON. Watch then covers 2187.5, 8414.5 and the other DSC frequencies.
Press '3 TEST' for the daily self test. Check ROM, RAM, LCD, KEY, TX, RX and 'DSC WATCH RX OK'.
Press '# SETUP' and select 'POSITION / TIME (GPS)' to check the position and UTC time.
Click 'BATTERY CHARGER' to switch it OFF. The 'IN USE' lamp lights.
Read the off-load voltage on the 'RADIO 24V BATT' volt meter.
Lift the handset and hold 'PTT' to read the on-load voltage and current.
Return 'BATTERY CHARGER' to AUTO and check the meters return to charging.
Press '1 RT/CH' (or '▶ Open RT/CH on the radio').
Turn the knob to scroll, or key in the channel or frequency (e.g. 8 0 1 or 8 2 9 4). '*' deletes a digit.
Press '#' to switch between J3E and H3E. Push the knob to set the frequency.
Press '0 TUNE'. Wait for 'TUNED SWR OK'. The radio will not transmit voice until tuned.
Distress RT is 2182.0 kHz (MF) and 8291.0 kHz (8 MHz). Never use 2187.5 or 8414.5 for routine calls.
Press '2 DSC' (or 'CALL') and select 'TEST CALL'.
'TO COAST STN' is 005480001. Select 'DSC FREQ' and push the knob to step through values (e.g. 2187.5 or 8414.5).
Move to '[ CALL ]' and push the knob. The display shows 'DSC TEST … kHz'.
Wait for 'TEST ACK' from the coast station. (On board) log the test call weekly.
Press '2 DSC', select 'DISTRESS MSG EDIT'. Set 'NATURE' ('Undesignated' or e.g. 'Fire / explosion').
Set 'FREQ' to 'Multi-frequency', '2187.5 single' or '8414.5 single'. Check 'POS', then select '[ SAVE ]'.
Click the cover to lift it. Press and hold 'DISTRESS' for 4 seconds until it lights steady.
Wait for 'DISTRESS ACK'. The radio sets RT 2182.0 kHz. Press 'CANCEL' to stop the alarm.
Lift the handset, build the MAYDAY message and hold 'PTT' to send on 2182.0 kHz.
MF alert ('MF distress (2187.5)'): press 'CANCEL' to stop the alarm. Do NOT press '5 ACK/SQ'.
Set RT to 2182.0 and press '0 TUNE'. Listen for the coast station.
If none acknowledges after 5 min (30 s here) and the ship is near, acknowledge by RT on 2182.
HF alert ('HF distress (8414.5)'): stop the alarm, do not acknowledge, listen on the RT frequency of that band.
If no coast station acknowledges after 5 min (30 s here), press '2 DSC' and select 'DISTRESS RELAY'.
Set 'TO' to '005480001 (CST)', never 'ALL SHIPS'. Keep 'DSC FREQ' 8414.5 and select '[ SEND ]'. Wait for 'RELAY ACK'.
If 'Coast station ACK of that distress' arrives first, no relay is needed: keep the RT watch.
Ship: '2 DSC' → 'INDIVIDUAL CALL', 'TO' '548777222 SHIP', 'DSC FREQ' '2177.0', 'WORK FREQ' intership (e.g. 8294.0).
Coast station: 'TO' '005480001 CST', 'DSC FREQ' '2189.5', 'WORK FREQ' a duplex channel such as 'CH 801'.
Select '[ CALL ]'. When the ACK shows 'Accept New Working Freq', push the knob to accept.
Press '0 TUNE', lift the handset and do a radio check on the working frequency.
Incoming call ('Individual call + working freq'): push the knob to accept 8255.0 kHz, then '0 TUNE'.
RT call on 2182 ('Ship calls you on 2182'): answer on 2182, agree 8294 kHz, set and tune it, call again.
'ALL SHIPS CALL' is SAFETY or URGENCY only; follow it by RT on 2182.
'Main power failure' sounds an alarm; the display shows 'PWR BATTERY' and the 'IN USE' lamp lights.
Press 'BUZZER STOP' to silence the alarm. The radio keeps working on the reserve battery.
Keep the DSC watch. Watch the volt meter; the 'LOW VOLT' lamp lights below about 23 V.
Limit transmissions while on battery. 'Restore power' returns 'PWR MAIN 24V'.
(On board) inform the OOW/ETO and log the failure and battery readings.

sections.h: Cancel false alert, log and close
steps: False alert: do not switch off. Press '2 DSC' and select 'DISTRESS CANCEL'.
The radio sets 2182.0 kHz. Send by RT: 'ALL STATIONS' ×3 … 'CANCEL MY DISTRESS ALERT OF…' '= MASTER…' 'OUT'.
Press '* FILE' to view 'FILE / LOG': received messages and sent calls with UTC times. '8 PRINT' prints.
(On board) copy all entries into the GMDSS radio logbook.
Put the handset back on hook. There is no power-off control; (on board) keep the DSC watch running at sea.

tips: Knob: mouse wheel or click its left/right side to turn; click the centre to push (ENT). Esc = 'CANCEL'.
In forms, pushing the knob on a field steps to its next value; move to the bracketed button to send or save.
A blinking 'NOT TUNED - 0:TUNE' means the RT frequency changed: press '0 TUNE' before talking.
Waiting times are shortened: 5 minutes is 30 seconds in this simulator.
'↺ RESET' clears everything and restarts the training tasks.

satc.title: Inmarsat-C Terminal

steps: The terminal is powered when the page opens; '↺ RESET TERMINAL' restarts it. The 'POWER' switch is not operable here.
Check the status screen: 'NO SYNC', 'LOGOUT' and 'Pos. age' showing 'OLD!' mean action is needed.
Open menus with F1–F10 on the keyboard or by clicking the menu bar. Arrow keys and Enter select; Esc closes.
Run 'F7 Options' → 'Self test'. Check the printout: ROM, RAM, PRINTER, GPS and ANTENNA OK.
Press F7 'Options' → 'Login…'. Choose 'Ocean region' IOR or POR (AOR fails here) and select 'LOGIN'.
Wait for 'Login acknowledged by NCS…'. The SYNC and LOGIN LEDs light and a default LES is set.
Press F8 'Setup' → 'Position (GPS / manual)…'. 'Source' GPS, select 'UPDATE'. Check 'Pos. age' resets.
Update the position at least every 4 hours if it is not automatic.
Before switching off or changing ocean region: F7 'Options' → 'Logout' and wait for 'Logout acknowledged'.
Press F9 'Distress' → 'Distress alert setup…'. Check 'LES', set 'Nature of distress', 'Course (°)', 'Speed (kn)'. Select 'SAVE'.
Undesignated alerts are allowed, but the terminal warns: set the nature if time permits.
Click the cover to lift it. Press and hold 'DISTRESS' 4 seconds while the hold bar fills.
'DISTRESS ALERT TRANSMITTED' appears and prints. Wait for 'DISTRESS ALERT ACKNOWLEDGED'.
Press F10 'StopAlarm' to silence the alarm. Check F6 'Logs' → 'Distress log'.
Press F1 'File' → 'New' and type the details: ship, position, nature, assistance needed, persons on board.
Press F3 (or F9 'Distress') → 'Distress priority message…'. Destination is 'RCC (via LES)', priority 'DISTRESS'.
Select 'SEND'. The terminal must be logged in.
Read the RCC reply in F6 'Logs' → 'Receive log'. Keep watch on VHF 16 / DSC as advised.
Press F1 'File' → 'New'. Type the message in the EDIT window.
Press F3 'Transmit' → 'Send message…'. Choose 'LES', 'Destination' (E-mail, Telex or Special access code).
Fill 'Address / number / code', set 'Delivery confirmation' Yes, and select 'SEND'.
Wait for 'Message … accepted by LES'. The delivery confirmation arrives in F6 'Logs' → 'Receive log'.
Position report: F5 'Reports' → 'Position report (code 43)…', or F2 'Edit' → 'Position report template'.
Medical advice: send with Special access code 32. Other codes: 38, 39, 41, 42, 43.
F1 'File' also offers 'Save', 'Open (saved / drafts)' and 'Print'.
Press F4 'EGC' → 'EGC setup (area)…'. Set 'NAVAREA / METAREA' to XI and 'Auto print' ON. Select 'SAVE'.
Warnings and forecasts for other areas are not received; distress and SAR broadcasts always are.
Open F4 'EGC' → 'EGC message log'. New messages are marked; click or Enter to read, 'PRINT' or 'CLOSE (Esc)'.
Urgent (piracy) and distress (SAR relay) EGCs sound an alarm. Press F10 'StopAlarm', then read the message.
SAR relay: keep a lookout, assist if possible, report to the RCC (code 39).
F7 'Options' → 'Link test' or 'PV test (perf. verification)'. Both need login and print the result.
The PV test includes a distress alert test in test mode — it is not a real alert.
Printer panel: 'ON LINE' toggles online/offline; 'LF' line feed; 'FF' form feed; 'NLQ' print quality; 'P.PARK' parks paper.
Offline jobs wait in a queue and print when you press 'ON LINE' again.
(On board) record tests in the GMDSS radio log.
'Antenna blocked (lose sync)': 'NO SYNC' and 'LOGOUT' show. After 'Restore all', log in again with F7.
'GPS failure': 'GPS Status' shows 'NO FIX'. Use F8 'Setup' → Position, 'Source' Manual, e.g. '14 30.20 N', '120 49.60 E'.
'Printer paper out': the P.OUT lamp lights. Load paper (on board), then press 'ON LINE' to print queued jobs.
False alert: do not switch off. F9 → 'Cancel a false alert (procedure)' shows the steps.
Write 'CANCEL MY INMARSAT-C DISTRESS ALERT OF…' with name, call sign, IMN, position; send as a distress priority message.
Wait for the RCC reply 'SAR action stood down'. Inform the Master and log it.
F6 'Logs' gives 'Transmit log', 'Receive log' and 'Distress log'. Open entries to read or print them.
Copy important entries into the GMDSS radio logbook (on board).
Log out with F7 'Options' → 'Logout'. (On board) only then switch the terminal off, as the manual allows.

tips: Messages cannot be sent before login; the terminal says 'NOT LOGGED IN'.
Watch the bottom line: 'POSITION NOT UPDATED' blinks when the position is older than 4 hours.
Instructor EGC buttons only work when the terminal has NCS sync.
Click the on-screen keyboard or type on your own keyboard in the EDIT window.

epirb.title: EPIRB (406 MHz)

steps: This is a step-by-step lesson, not a free-running panel. Use 'NEXT ▶' and '◀ BACK', or click a lesson tab.
A lesson tab turns green when its task is complete. 'START AGAIN' resets everything.
Lessons 1, 2 and 6 explain the EPIRB, how the alert travels and the signals (406 MHz, 121.5 MHz, AIS, strobe).

sections.h: Know the parts and expiry dates
steps: Open '3  The parts' and click all 9 numbered parts.
Note part 5, the mode switch: READY in the bracket, TEST for self-test, OFF only for transport or servicing.
Note part 8, the battery expiry label: renew the battery before this date (usually 5 years).
Open '4  Float-free and HRU'. The HRU releases at about 1.5–4 m; check its expiry date (usually every 2 years).
Never paint over the bracket or lash the EPIRB down.
Open '8  Monthly check and test'. Click each step in the list in order.
Check bracket, switch READY, cover closed, no damage, strobe lens clean.
Check the battery and HRU expiry dates, the lanyard (not tied to the ship) and the identity label.
At the self-test step, click 'SWITCH TO TEST'. The indicator shows amber: self-test running.
Wait for green (PASS), then click the next step to return the switch to READY.
Click the last step to record the test in the GMDSS radio log.
Open '5  Manual activation'. Use only in real distress or when abandoning ship.
Click 'PULL SAFETY PIN'. (On board) first take the EPIRB out of its bracket.
Click 'PUSH (hold 1 s)'. The strobe and indicator flash: 406 MHz alert and 121.5 MHz homing are sent.
(On board) tie the lanyard to the survival craft, never the ship, and let the EPIRB float upright.
Leave it ON until rescued. 'RESET' returns the beacon to the bracket state.
Open '7  Identity and registration' and compare the label with the sample registration record.
Check the 15-character HEX ID, MMSI, vessel name, call sign and 'VALID TO' date match the ship.
(On board) re-code and re-register if the name, flag, MMSI or owner changes.
Open '9  False alert'. Click the buttons in order.
Click '1  SWITCH OFF' (or return it to READY in the bracket, per the manual).
Click '2  INFORM RCC / COAST STATION': name, MMSI, HEX ID, time, position, 'no distress'.
Click '3  LOG ENTRY' to record it in the GMDSS radio log.
'SWITCH OFF' in lesson 5 also warns: switch off only after a false alert, and tell the RCC.
Open '10  Quiz' and answer all 10 questions. 8 or more correct is a pass.
Read 'Real and simplified' at the end, then click 'NEXT ▶' to finish the course.

tips: This simulator has no failure or instructor buttons; tasks must be done in order or a warning appears.
The ECADEMY E-1 is a generic model: real switch names and test patterns differ by maker.
Annual test and 5-yearly shore-based maintenance are done by approved staff (on board: check the certificates).

sart.title: SART (Radar Transponder)

steps: This is a step-by-step lesson. Use 'NEXT ▶' and '◀ BACK', or click a lesson tab. 'START AGAIN' resets.
Lesson 1 shows the SART and its 12-dot reply on a rescue ship's radar.
In '2  Alerting and locating', click 'ALERTING (EPIRB)' or 'LOCATING (SART)' to compare; 'REPLAY' restarts the animation.
